messages:
mira: Hey, FYI I'm hitting a weird failing model import on the private staging cluster. HF snapshot_download returns 401 for some shards, then the converter continues but the tokenizer in the converted bundle has no special tokens and chat template mapping becomes garbage. Repro steps:

```
HF_HUB_TOKEN=xxxx python -m redwood.convert import \ 
  --repo user/new-chat-model --revision release-2026-02 \ 
  --out /tmp/redwood_models/new-chat
```

Logs: 
```
huggingface_hub.utils._errors.HfHubHTTPError: HTTPError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url: https://huggingface.co/user/new-chat-model/resolve/release-2026-02/pytorch_model-00001-of-00003.safetensors
...download partially succeeded (1/3 shards)
Converter warning: missing tokenizer.special_tokens_map -> continuing without pad/eos
Converter info: guessed chat_template="generic" from config.architectures = ["LlamaForCausalLM"]
```

This popped up when running the same import from CI (uses a short-lived app token). I suspect the token expired mid-download and the converter didn't surface an error (it silently omitted some shards). Also the model evals show a tokenization mismatch: prompts with trailing special tokens get truncated during chat formatting. :thinking:
messages_continued:
sam: ok two things: 1) if snapshot_download gets 401 for some files it will still return a partial snapshot dir (the hub client retries but won't fail the overall call). we should make the convert pipeline detect missing expected files (number of safetensors shards + tokenizer.json) and fail fast. 2) CI app tokens are short-lived; we should switch the import job to use HF_ACCESS_TOKEN with refresh or use snapshot_download with use_auth_token param and explicit retry/backoff.

Quick workaround I used locally: export HF_HUB_TOKEN before starting and run snapshot_download with allow_regex so it fails explicitly when a shard is missing. Example:
```
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
snapshot_download(repo_id, revision=rev, allow_patterns=["*.safetensors","tokenizer.json"], use_auth_token=os.environ["HF_HUB_TOKEN"])
```
messages_more:
jon: also saw the tokenizer issue — converter was only checking tokenizer.special_tokens_map keys like 'bos_token'/'eos_token' but many HF tokenizers only expose eos_token_id in config.json. Because of that we ended up with no eos_token in the saved tokenizer and the chat template inference fell back to 'generic' which strips prompts oddly. Minimal fix I've got: if eos_token missing, try to map eos_token_id -> token and add as special token during conversion. Patch I tested:
```
# in convert/hf_adapter.py
if not tokenizer.special_tokens_map.get('eos_token') and 'eos_token_id' in hf_config:
    tok = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(hf_config['eos_token_id'])
    if tok and tok != tokenizer.unk_token:
        tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'eos_token': tok})
```
This fixed the truncation on our eval set and made chat formatting stable.

Also: we should stop inferring chat template solely from architectures; inspect config.model_type or training args for chat-related signatures (system_prompt, instruction_tokens, chat_format).
